For this assignment, create an HTML page using Quarto. You can refer to the [homepage.qmd](https://github.com/bsmity13/BCB5200/blob/main/code/homepage.qmd) document document we created in class for some ideas.

- Make sure your YAML header has:
  - The option `embed-resources: true`
    - This goes under the html: format option.
    - It will make sure the HTML file stands alone, rather than referring to an external figure. I won't be able to see your figure if you upload and HTML file without this option.
- I want to see the code chunks that create your figure, so make sure you use `#| echo: true` in your R code chunk.
  - You may use code folding (`#| code-fold: true`) if you'd like.
    
The purpose of this assignment is gain some familiarity creating data visualizations using `ggplot2`. You can refer to the script we wrote in class for some ideas.

## Instructions

1. Find a dataset.
2. Write a *small* amount of narrative in your Quarto document about the dataset and why you want to make a particular visualization. *Don't spend a lot of time on the narrative.*
3. Create at least two figures. For at least one of them, pipe (`%>%` or `|>`) the data to `ggplot()` after manipulating the `data.frame`. Each figure should use at least 3 channels (*e.g.*, x-axis, y-axis, color/shape/size). Make sure the figure has a legend!

Let me know if you have any questions!
